subject: Need help with constant BFMI Low

messages.author: 4a2e2255c743da08
messages.subject: Need help with constant BFMI Low
parts:
Hi there,

I am doing a simple spatial hierarchical model to estimate population by states. Attached is the data. I look on the debug in stan website and try to reparamerization and still have the following error. Any help is greatly appreciated! Thanks!!!

The model is to estimate the state population where each state ties to a division (hierachical).

Warnings:
Warning messages:
1: There were 17 divergent transitions after warmup. Increasing adapt_delta above 0.99 may help. See
http://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#divergent-transitions-after-warmup 
2: There were 4 chains where the estimated Bayesian Fraction of Missing Information was low. See
http://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#bfmi-low 
3: Examine the pairs() plot to diagnose sampling problems


Code:
model_stan = "
data {
  int<lower=1> n; 
int<lower=1> ndivisions; 
real y[n];
int<lower=1, upper = ndivisions> division[n];
real a;
real k;
real l;
real m;
}

parameters {
real eta;
real <lower=0> sigma_c;
real <lower=0> sigma_s;
real <lower=0> sigma_r;
real <lower=0> theta[n];
real <lower=0> mu[ndivisions];
}


model {

for(i in 1:n){
y[i] ~ normal (theta[mu[i]],sigma_c);
}

theta ~ normal (mu[division],sigma_s);
mu ~ normal(eta,sigma_r);

sigma_c ~ cauchy(a,k);
sigma_s ~ cauchy(a,l);
sigma_r ~ cauchy(a,m);
}
"
m = stan_model(model_code=model_stan)

dat = list(n=nrow(pop), ndivisions = nlevels(pop$DIVISION), y = log10(pop$POPESTIMATE2016), division = as.numeric(pop$DIVISION), a = 0, k = 0.1, l = 0.1,m = 0.1)
r = sampling(m, dat,iter=2000, control = list(adapt_delta=0.99))
r

messages.author: 4a2e2255c743da08
messages.subject: Re: Need help with constant BFMI Low
parts: I tried couple things this morning. Have my prior cauchy std = 1 and added "stepsize = 0.01, max_treedepth =15" into the control. I still get the warnings but my rhat is between 1 to 1.03. As I read couple other posts, someone mentioned that if I can ignore these warnings if my rhat is close to 1? Is that true? Thanks!

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Need help with constant BFMI Low
parts:
The divergences are your top priority so start by playing
with adapt_delta.  And make sure that you run multiple
chains.  You will probably need to look at a non-centered
parameterization.
On Apr 27, 2017, at 2:46 PM, Lawrence Hii <lawrenc...@gmail.com> wrote:
